turnaround_reason: Fox Factory was crushed by a post-COVID bike-industry inventory glut and soft powersports/OEM demand, driving revenue down and pushing the stock to ~$13 lows. It is now recovering (+16% over 30d) on two straight strong earnings beats, a raised full-year sales outlook, and 22.5% powersports growth.
bullish_points: Two consecutive large beats: Q2 2026 EPS $0.37 vs $0.18 est (+107%), Q1 $0.18 vs $0.08 (+120%); adjusted EBITDA ~$5M above the high end of Q2 guide
Management raised FY sales guidance to $1.42B-$1.47B and points to H2 margin expansion from cost optimization and tariff anniversary benefits
Powersports segment soaring (+22.5%) and bike demand stabilizing with new e-bike and softball (Marucci) product launches
Diversified brand portfolio (FOX, Marzocchi, Race Face, Marucci, Method) across powered vehicles, aftermarket, and specialty sports
Reasonable valuation for a recovering cyclical: EV/EBITDA ~10.6, forward P/E ~11.7
bearish_points: Input-cost inflation running ~$20M above plan (steel, aluminum, freight, fuel) pressuring the margin-recovery thesis
Specialty Sports Group / bike remains volatile and the recovery there is 'stabilization,' not growth
Leverage is elevated: D/E ~102%, total debt $680M vs $61M cash; profit margin still negative (-20.4% TTM, GAAP hit by non-cash items)
Consumer-cyclical demand (premium bikes, powersports) is discretionary and rate/consumer-sentiment sensitive
Insider activity is grants only — no open-market conviction buying
catalyst: Continued earnings beats and the H2 2026 margin-expansion inflection as tariff/cost comparisons ease; FY guidance raises
suggested_trade: Spot, small-to-medium starter around current levels; add on a confirmed H2 margin-expansion print. Options OI is thin (88 calls / 10 puts) so prefer shares
key_risk: Bike demand relapses or input-cost inflation overwhelms the cost-savings program, so the raised guidance proves too optimistic and the multiple re-rates down
would_skip_if: Q3 shows margin compression despite the tariff anniversary, or bike/powersports orders roll over again
